name: Leucodontaceae

lineage_context.teaching_goal: Teach Leucodon julaceus as a pleurocarpous bark/rock moss with glossy cylindrical julaceous branches, tightly appressed ecostate leaves and exserted symmetric capsules.

project_scope.note: Leucodon julaceus is accepted in FNA/WFO and FNA includes Texas.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: Read the branch silhouette before individual leaves. Leucodon julaceus often forms short curved cylindrical catkin-like branches because its overlapping leaves stay erect-appressed.
family_diagnostics.gametophyte: Pleurocarpous moss on bark, logs, rock or soil; plants medium-sized and often somewhat glossy. Branches typically short, curved and julaceous.
family_diagnostics.leaf_anatomy: Branch leaves overlap tightly, are not plicate in the project species, and lack a costa (ecostate).
family_diagnostics.sporophyte: Capsules are symmetric, ovoid-cylindric and usually exserted beyond the perichaetial leaves; calyptra can split along one side and temporarily clasp the seta/capsule.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Creeping bark/rock moss + glossy cylindrical julaceous branches + tightly appressed ecostate leaves = project Leucodontaceae/Leucodon.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: substrate/habit → julaceous branch → appressed ecostate leaf → capsule/calyptra → acrocarp-vs-pleurocarp comparison
visual_lesson.intro: Leucodon is easiest to recognize as architecture: its short branches look like tiny smooth catkins because the leaves overlap tightly around the stem.

steps.title: 1 · Find the cylindrical branch
steps.look_for: Short curved branch with leaves packed around the stem, giving a smooth wormlike/catkin-like profile.
steps.why_it_matters: This is the meaning of julaceous and the best visual memory cue.

steps.title: 2 · Pull off one leaf and look for no costa
steps.look_for: No central costa running through the leaf.
steps.why_it_matters: Leucodon is characteristically ecostate and this separates it from many robust moss lookalikes.

steps.title: 3 · Check whether the leaves are plicate
steps.look_for: Project L. julaceus leaves remain comparatively smooth rather than strongly longitudinally folded.
steps.why_it_matters: FNA separates L. julaceus from related Leucodon species partly by its non-plicate leaves.

steps.title: 4 · See the capsule clear the branch leaves
steps.look_for: Ovoid-cylindric symmetric capsule barely to clearly exserted above the perichaetial leaves.

steps.title: 5 · Contrast growth architecture
steps.look_for: Leucodon pleurocarpous creeping system with lateral branches versus Leucobryum/Pottiaceae upright acrocarpous cushions/turfs.
steps.why_it_matters: Teaches moss growth form as a higher-level ID tool.

comparisons.title: Leucodontaceae vs Leucobryaceae
comparisons.rule: Leucodon is a pleurocarpous bark/rock moss with julaceous branches and ecostate leaves. Leucobryum is an upright pale cushion moss whose leaves are dominated by a broad leucocyst-rich costa.

comparisons.title: Leucodontaceae vs Pottiaceae
comparisons.rule: Leucodon branch leaves overlap tightly and lack a costa; the project Pottiaceae concept is acrocarpous with a strong costa, papillose cells and conspicuously crisp/squarrose leaves.

visual_lesson.caveat: The cylindrical branch silhouette is highly useful but not unique to one species. Confirm the ecostate, non-plicate leaf and sporophyte characters when a species-level call matters.

genera.fast_cue: glossy pleurocarp + short curved julaceous branches + appressed ecostate leaves

taxonomy_reconciliation.note: Accepted in current WFO/FNA; FNA distribution includes Texas.

visual_targets.annotation_goal: label branch axis and tightly imbricate leaves
compare smooth leaf surface with plicate Leucodon lookalike
label capsule, seta and perichaetial leaves
